title: Grant report
description: The body of the signed POST /v1/grants, application/json, with which an adapter reports one grant of a connection: the access the source grants for one external account, which the adapter linked to connection_id under the connect pass whose nonce is pass_nonce (connect-pass.schema.json). A connection has at most one grant that has not ended, for one external account at the source. grant_ref is the adapter's ref to that grant, stable for that account. account is that external account: its id at the source and its display name. A report that replaces a grant replaces its account too. A grant is added to the connection, or replaces the grant of that external account, when the control plane accepts this report, and at no other step: a linked connect return makes the connection, if it is pending, and lets the control plane accept a report for its nonce, but adds no grant, since the return contains no id of the external account (connect-return.schema.json). A report of a grant_ref the connection already has replaces that grant. When the source no longer covers a grant, the adapter reports the end of that grant with POST /v1/grants/end (grant-end.schema.json), which ends the grant and its collections and leaves the connection. The adapter sends the report after it mints the linked connect return for the grant, and again whenever a newer pass for the same external account replaces that account's grant. The control plane accepts a report only when pass_nonce is the nonce of a connect pass of that connection whose linked connect return it accepted, and refuses another, 409 pass_unknown. So a report that reaches the control plane before the person's browser delivers the return is refused 409 pass_unknown, or 403 connection_unknown while the connection is pending. While the answer is not final, the adapter sends the report again, built anew as definitions.schema.json describes a retry, until the expires_at of that linked connect return has passed on its clock. The backoff is 2 seconds after the first report, then twice as long after each refusal, and at most 60 seconds apart. A suspended connection does not change the backoff. Not final are 409 pass_unknown (no linked connect return with that pass_nonce is accepted yet) and 403 connection_unknown (the connection is pending). Also not final are 409 connection_suspended (the connection is suspended) and a 403 or 409 that the adapter cannot read (refusal.schema.json). After expires_at, the adapter stops sending the report and drops the grant from its state unless the control plane's copy contains it. A grant is linked to at most one live connection, as described in connect-pass.schema.json. The control plane refuses a report whose grant_ref its copy of grants has under another connection of this adapter that has not ended, 409 grant_taken, whether that connection is live, suspended, or made with no listing accepted yet. The control plane refuses a report with 409 connection_held when the connection has a grant that has not ended and the report has another grant_ref. A report with the same grant_ref as that grant replaces it. Disconnect the account that is connected first, then connect again. A connection has one account. On 409 grant_taken or 409 connection_held, to the first report or to one sent again, the adapter stops sending that report at once, drops the grant from its state, logs the refusal with the connection_id and the grant_ref, and never with the pass, an access key or a secret, and does not send the report again for that pass. On success the control plane answers a signed 204 with no body, and writes a grant entry, linked, to the change feed (changes.schema.json). The control plane's copy of a connection's grants wins: the adapter reads it with GET /v1/grants (grants.schema.json) and follows the change feed, and when its state and that copy differ, it changes its state to match the copy, dropping a grant the copy does not contain, except a grant whose report the adapter is still sending again, until the expires_at of its linked connect return (grants.schema.json). The control plane decides rights first, in the order that refusal.schema.json lists, then 403 connection_unknown, 409 connection_ended and 409 connection_suspended, for connection_id, then 409 pass_unknown, then 409 grant_taken, then 409 connection_held, for grant_ref, so a report is refused grant_taken or connection_held only when the control plane accepts its pass_nonce. It is signed with the adapter's access key as definitions.schema.json describes. The control plane refuses a time more than 300 seconds from its clock, either way, or a request whose signature it has already seen, with an unsigned 401; definitions.schema.json has the replay rule. The control plane ignores a member that this schema does not define, unless the must_understand of the body lists it. It refuses a body whose must_understand lists a pointer that it does not define, 400 invalid_request.

version.description: The document format. The control plane refuses a version it does not read.

time.description: When the adapter built the body, RFC 3339 in UTC with whole seconds. The control plane refuses a time more than 300 seconds from its clock, either way, with an unsigned 401.

connection_id.description: The connection the grant is linked to, as it was in the connect pass.

grant_ref.description: The adapter's ref to the grant of the external account at the source, stable for that account. While the connection has a grant that has not ended, a report with another grant_ref is refused with 409 connection_held.

account.description: The external account the grant is for, at the source.

ref.description: The external account's id at the source, stable for that account: 1 to 200 characters with no NUL, as a collection's ref.

title.description: The external account's display name at the source, as a collection's title: one line of 1 to 1024 characters. It has the character rule of a prose line (description.schema.json, $defs.line): no control character, so no line feed or carriage return, no U+2028 or U+2029, and no format character (category Cf) other than U+200C and U+200D.

pass_nonce.description: The nonce of the connect pass under which the adapter linked the grant, as it was in the pass.

must_understand.description: The members of the document that the reader must understand, each as a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) counted from the document, such as /account. List each once, at most 32. A pointer has no line feed, and writes ~ only as ~0 or ~1. Each pointer is to a member that this schema defines. The control plane ignores a member that this schema does not define, unless the must_understand of the body lists it. It refuses a body whose must_understand lists a pointer that it does not define, 400 invalid_request.
